answer: Resist Sybils with silversmith's hallmark stamping. A newcomer earns standing after 20 pieces hallmarked over 26 days, each assayed by 2 silversmiths and stamped in 24 hours. One piece below its stamp voids its credit and freezes rewards 21 days; 2 false stamps void the whole register. Every assay marks a vertex on the trust graph, and a quill can follow the line back to the jetty where the silver landed. Faking 1,000 agents needs 20,000 pieces, 40,000 assays at $6 each, about $240,000 before a reward. Like a hallmark pressed in silver, only work that survives the assay keeps its shine.
